title: Criteria to Distinguish Prohibited Political Advocacy from Expressions of Humanitarian Concern in Assessing Artists’ Conduct Relating to International Conflicts
what_it_is: Criteria to Distinguish Prohibited Political Advocacy from Expressions of Humanitarian Concern in Assessing Artists’ Conduct Relating to International Conflicts

sections.label: Humanitarian concerns and public order
sections.summary: Humanitarian concerns must not undermine public order, national security or stability, and foreigners must not use Singapore for political causes.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for Digital Development and Information)
sentences.text: While humanitarian concerns can be expressed in different ways, it should not undermine public order, national security or stability in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for Digital Development and Information)
sentences.text: This condition is made clear in the Arts Entertainment Classification Code issued by the Infocomm Media Development Authority (IMDA), which all licensees are required to comply with.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for Digital Development and Information)
sentences.text: Moreover, Singapore should not be used by foreigners as a platform to further political causes, including those relating to conflicts or political issues overseas.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for Digital Development and Information)
sentences.text: Besides the intent of their actions, IMDA will consider the likely impact of their performance to assess if the conditions are met.

sections.label: Line crossed by conduct
sections.summary: The line is crossed when conduct or content undermines public order, national security or stability, or foreigners use Singapore for political causes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: The line is crossed when conduct or content undermines public order, national security or stability, or where foreigners use Singapore as a platform to further political causes.

sections.label: Examples of classified events
sections.summary: Examples include an R18 variety event, a play on genocide themes, and an Advisory 16 comedy tour segment on the Israel-Gaza conflict.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: For example, on 16 May 2026, an event called "To The Unforgotten", a variety event, classified R18, some mature content.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: It featured a song, poem and multimedia on the Israel-Gaza conflict.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: And we have another example, it was a play, "6 Microlectures on Genocides".

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: The play comprised short works that explore themes of genocide, war crimes and contemporary conflicts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: And another example is a stand-up comedy tour called "Namaste", a couple of years ago in September 2024, classified Advisory 16, some mature content and coarse language, and contained a segment where the comedian spoke about the Israel-Gaza conflict.
